problems: The blind guess (kettle or watering can with a long curved spout) only partly matches. The figure reads as a hook hanging over a round pot, not a spout pouring from a vessel. The gooseneck-kettle alternative is closer than the primary guess, since the round base and upward neck do resemble a kettle.
Label collisions: 'arm, inner' overlaps 'far tip of the arm' near the right end of the arm, and 'crown of the bend' sits on top of 'dip of the back'. Both are hard to read.
'left rim corner' label runs across the blue silhouette line and the gold line.

The gold skeleton runs diagonally from the hook tip to the left rim corner, cutting across the hook's vertical drop instead of following it. The gold lines read as a separate construction rather than part of the silhouette.

Stars are mostly on their parts: far arm tip, inner arm, crown of the bend, dip of the back, apex of the curl, long left drop, hook tip, and the pot rim and wall stars all sit near the correct spots. The figure is upright and the silhouette is a real outline, not a copy of the gold lines.
Scattered unlabelled white dots (left of the pot and below it) add noise and do not belong to the figure.
output.advice: Redraw is needed mainly for legibility, not star placement. (1) Separate the two arm-end labels: put 'far tip of the arm' above or right of star 93026 and put 'arm, inner' below star 93429. (2) Move 'dip of the back' (star 95066) below the back line so it no longer collides with 'crown of the bend' (93805). (3) Move 'left rim corner' (96950) to the left of the pot, off the outline. (4) Route the gold skeleton along the hook's vertical drop from 96483 to 96327 rather than as a diagonal cut to the rim, so the hook reads as a hook. (5) Remove or hide the stray unlabelled dots. (6) Consider adding a visual cue that the hook hangs from a crane or bar, so the figure reads as a pot hook and is less likely to be taken for a kettle spout. Keep the upright orientation and the blue silhouette as they are.
